name: Paper Plane
preparation: Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker filled with ice. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds until thoroughly chilled and aerated. Double strain into a chilled coupe glass.
description: Created in 2008 by modern cocktail pioneer Sam Ross for Chicago's The Violet Hour, the Paper Plane is an equal-parts modern masterpiece. Named after the M.I.A. song "Paper Planes", it achieves a sublime, palate-cleansing equilibrium between warm bourbon oak, the bittersweet orange and gentian of Aperol, the alpine herbal elegance of Amaro Nonino, and tart lemon juice.
garnish: Expressed lemon peel or miniature paper plane

name: The Division Bell
preparation: Add all ingredients into a shaker with ice. Shake hard and strain into a chilled coupe. Smoky, floral, and bright.
description: Invented in 2009 by Phil Ward at New York City's renowned mezcal haven Mayahuel, this drink is a bittersweet, smoky variation of the Last Word family. Mal Bien Mezcal's earthy campfire smoke and vegetal agave are illuminated by the citrusy gentian of Aperol and the deep marasca cherry and stone-fruit aroma of Luxardo Maraschino.

name: Hemingway Daiquiri
ingredients: 1/2 oz Fresh Grapefruit Juice (or 1/4 oz simple syrup)
preparation: Combine all ingredients in a cocktail shaker with ice. Shake hard for 12 seconds and fine strain into a coupe. Probitas rum provides the perfect balance of Barbados pot-still funk and Jamaican character.
description: Adapted from Ernest Hemingway’s customary order at Havana's El Floridita ("Papa Doble"), this refined version replaces added sugar with a splash of Luxardo Maraschino liqueur and fresh grapefruit juice. The grassy, ester-rich profile and tropical Jamaican funk of Probitas rum provide the ideal backbone for this crisp, bone-dry classic.
garnish: Lime wheel and Luxardo maraschino cherry

name: Mezcalita (Mezcal Margarita)
preparation: Shake with plenty of ice and strain into an ice-filled rocks glass with a salted rim.
description: An earthy, terroir-driven reimagining of the classic Margarita. Replacing tequila with Mal Bien Espadín brings savory complexity and sweet woodsmoke, perfectly cut by the sweet and bitter orange peel oils in Cointreau and crisp fresh lime juice.
garnish: Half-salted or Tajín rim, fresh lime wheel

name: Classic Daiquiri
preparation: Shake vigorously with ice and double strain into a chilled coupe glass.
description: The quintessential Cuban sour and the ultimate litmus test for any quality rum. Blending pot-still Jamaican and heritage Barbadian distillates, Probitas delivers pastry notes, vanilla, and overripe banana that cut cleanly through tart lime and gentle sweetness.

name: Classic Sidecar
preparation: Coat half the rim of a coupe in fine sugar. Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into the prepared glass.
description: A Roaring Twenties staple tracing back to Harry's New York Bar in Paris. E&J Brandy lends warmth and stewed fruit notes, which sparkle alongside the fragrant orange perfume of Cointreau and a crisp lemon snap, finished by a crystalline sugar rim.

name: White Lady
ingredients: Optional: 1 egg white (or 1/2 oz aquafaba) for a silky head
preparation: If using egg white, dry shake without ice first. Add ice, shake hard, and double strain into a coupe.
description: Popularized by bartender Harry Craddock at London's Savoy American Bar in the late 1920s, the White Lady is a pristine, zesty gin sour. Crisp botanical gin combines with dry curaçao and lemon; an optional egg white delivers a luscious, velvety foam top.

name: Japanese Slipper
preparation: Shake with ice and strain into a chilled coupe. A neon green, surprisingly tart and balanced 1980s modern classic.
description: Created in 1984 by Jean-Paul Bourguignon at Mietta's in Melbourne, Australia. While its radioactive neon-green appearance nods to 1980s cocktail maximalism, the equal-parts ratio delivers an unexpectedly sophisticated, refreshing balance of sweet honeydew, tart citrus, and orange liqueur.

name: Nonino Sour
preparation: Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
description: A soothing, complex digestif sour that lets the grappa-based Amaro Nonino take center stage. Notes of candied orange zest, licorice, and alpine botanicals meld with rich brandy and citrus for an exceptionally smooth, comforting sipper.

name: Boulevardier
preparation: Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass filled with ice. Stir for 30 seconds until cold and diluted. Strain over a large clear ice cube.
description: Conceived during American Prohibition by expatriate writer Erskine Gwynne in Paris and documented in 1927's Barflies and Cocktails. By trading gin for whiskey, the Negroni is transformed into a rich, autumnal cocktail with deep notes of vanilla, oak, and dark cocoa from the Carpano Antica vermouth.

name: Classic Negroni & Mezcal Negroni
ingredients: 1 oz Gin (or Mal Bien Mezcal for an earthier, smoky profile)
preparation: Stir ingredients with ice for 30 seconds. Strain over a large ice cube in an old fashioned glass.
description: The gold standard of Italian aperitivi, dating back to Florence circa 1919. Equal parts spirit, bitter liqueur, and vermouth create an intoxicating balance of bittersweet botanical majesty. Swapping gin for Mal Bien Mezcal yields a deeply smoky, savory Oaxacan riff.

name: Kingston Negroni
preparation: Stir with ice and strain over a large rock. The ester profile and oak aging of Probitas create an uncommonly rich negroni variant.
description: Popularized by bartender Joaquín Simó at Death & Co, this rum-centric Negroni swaps gin for a flavorful, unaged or lightly aged pot-still rum. Probitas rum’s tropical fruit, grassy cane, and rich mouthfeel harmonize effortlessly against the intense gentian bitterness of Campari and vanilla-forward Carpano Antica.

name: The Martinez
preparation: Stir with ice until thoroughly chilled and strain into a chilled coupe.
description: Widely celebrated as the direct precursor to the modern Martini, dating to O.H. Byron's 1884 bar manual. Dominated by rich sweet vermouth rather than gin, it possesses an antique, aromatic depth elevated by subtle cherry and almond notes from Luxardo Maraschino.

name: Classic Manhattan
preparation: Stir with ice in a mixing glass. Strain into a chilled coupe.
description: Born at New York's Manhattan Club in the 1870s, this spirit-forward staple showcases whiskey cushioned by the luscious, herbal vanilla of Carpano Antica Formula, accented by a barspoon of rich cherry syrup.

name: Left Hand
preparation: Sam Ross's famed Milk & Honey creation. Stir with ice and strain into a chilled coupe.
description: Crafted by Milk & Honey bartender Sam Ross, this variation takes the Boulevardier and adds a subtle kiss of chocolate liqueur. The baking spices, vanilla, and dark fruit in Carpano Antica form a natural bridge between whiskey, bitter Campari, and rich cacao.

name: Smoky Chocolate Negroni
preparation: Stir with ice in a mixing glass and strain over a single large ice cube. The earthy smoke of mezcal and dark cocoa create an extraordinary pairing.
description: Chocolate and roasted agave share ancient roots in Mexican culinary heritage. Here, mezcal's pungent minerality and campfire smoke are rounded out by the decadence of cacao, balanced by the bitter botanical snap of Campari and Carpano Antica vermouth.

name: Brandy Alexander
preparation: Shake vigorously with ice to aerate the cream. Double strain into a chilled coupe and dust liberally with nutmeg.
description: A luscious 1920s dessert cocktail that became an international sensation during the mid-century. Brandy cuts through velvety sweet cream and cacao, topped off with a dusting of spicy grated nutmeg for an indulgent evening treat.

name: 20th Century
preparation: Shake with ice and double strain into a chilled coupe.
description: Named after the famed 20th Century Limited luxury passenger train between New York and Chicago in 1937. It pairs botanical gin with fresh lemon and a subtle chocolate foundation from crème de cacao, yielding an unexpectedly crisp, bright drink.

name: Nonino & Cacao Nightcap
preparation: Stir with ice and pour over crushed ice or a large rock.
description: An opulent dessert digestif that highlights Amaro Nonino’s baked orange peel and herb notes alongside the velvety warmth of chocolate and oak-aged spirit.

name: Andean Highball / Matacuy Spritz
ingredients: 4 oz Club Soda or Premium Tonic Water
preparation: Fill a tall glass with ice. Pour in Matacuy and top with chilled club soda or tonic. Stir gently once to combine. Highlights the wild Andean botanicals and minty muña character.
description: A tall, effervescent showcase of Peru's Matacuy Elixir Andino. Made in the Sacred Valley with wild Andean botanicals, its dominant character of muña (Andean mountain mint) blooms when lengthened with cold soda water or tonic, making for an invigorating herbal highball.
garnish: Fresh mint sprig or lime wheel
